article: Better safe than sorry, eh? Canada’s modernized antitrust and marketing framework
stem: A multinational company faces an organization with overlapping compliance responsibilities and inconsistent control ownership. Which action should its chief compliance officer prioritize to improve program design?
options: Map the workflow, clarify accountable owners and handoffs, then evaluate the controls using design walkthroughs and responsible managers’ attestations.
Assign every control to compliance irrespective of operational ownership.
Introduce a new tool before identifying the source of process failure.
Map the workflow, clarify accountable owners and handoffs, then test the controls against real cases.
explanation: The best choice is to map the workflow, clarify accountable owners and handoffs, then test the controls against real cases. This approach focuses on program design rather than relying on an untested shortcut. The other options either substitute assertions for evidence, postpone assessment, or weaken accountability. Tailor instruction to role-based risks and test whether employees can apply it in realistic decisions.
Increase the number of slides while retaining the same generic annual module.
Consider training effective solely because completion rates exceed the target.
explanation: The best choice is to tailor instruction to role-based risks and test whether employees can apply it in realistic decisions. This approach focuses on training effectiveness rather than relying on an untested shortcut. The other options either substitute assertions for evidence, postpone assessment, or weaken accountability. Editorial basis: CEP 2026-09, Stop asking “Any questions?”: How to make compliance training land, p. 59; verify the precise article passage before using this in a scored mock exam.
